nodes.name: Colloidal Synthesis VSe2
nodes.procedure: The synthetic procedure was conducted using the Schlenk line under N2 flow. In the colloidal synthesis, 10mL of oleylamine (technical grade 80%) and 5mL octadecene (technical grade 90%) in a three-necked flask were degassed at 150°C for 20 min then the temperature was raised to 280°C. 1.0mmol of VCl3 (technical grade 95%) and 0.5mmol of (PhCH2)2Se2 (98%) were dissolved in 5mL oleylamine and the mixture was kept at 60°C for 30 min. The above mixture was injected into the above heated three-necked flask relaxedly in 10 min. After 30 min reaction, the reaction solution was cooled down to 60°C, and the products were washed with cyclohexane for three times. The black powder was placed in a quartz tube inside an electrically heated furnace and annealed under N2 flow at 400°C for 2h.

nodes.name: Colloidal Synthesis V0.8Mo0.2Se2
nodes.procedure: The mixture of VCl3 (0.8mmol) and MoCl5 (0.2mmol) was employed as di-metal sources to obtain V0.8Mo0.2Se2 nanoflakes under the same synthetic process as VSe2: 10mL of oleylamine (technical grade 80%) and 5mL octadecene (technical grade 90%) in a three-necked flask were degassed at 150°C for 20 min then the temperature was raised to 280°C under N2 flow. The mixture was dissolved in 5mL oleylamine and kept at 60°C for 30 min. The above mixture was injected into the heated three-necked flask relaxedly in 10 min. After 30 min reaction at 280°C, the reaction solution was cooled down to 60°C, and the products were washed with cyclohexane for three times. The black powder was annealed under N2 flow at 400°C for 2h.

nodes.name: H2O2 Corrosion VSe2-x
nodes.procedure: Twenty milligrams of VSe2 nanoflakes were immersed in 1.2 molL-1 H2O2 solution (20 mL) with a magnetic stirrer and the temperature of the solution was kept at 60°C. After 3 min corrosion, the precipitate was filtered, washed with deionized water for three times, and dried in a vacuum at 50°C for 12 h.

nodes.name: Colloidal Synthesis MoSe2
nodes.procedure: Pure MoSe2 sample can also be prepared through this colloidal process when 1.0mmol of VCl3 was replaced by 0.5mmol MoCl5: 10mL of oleylamine (technical grade 80%) and 5mL octadecene (technical grade 90%) in a three-necked flask were degassed at 150°C for 20 min then the temperature was raised to 280°C. 0.5mmol of MoCl5 and 0.5mmol of (PhCH2)2Se2 (98%) were dissolved in 5mL oleylamine and the mixture was kept at 60°C for 30 min. The above mixture was injected into the above heated three-necked flask relaxedly in 10 min. After 30 min reaction, the reaction solution was cooled down to 60°C, and the products were washed with cyclohexane for three times. The black powder was placed in a quartz tube inside an electrically heated furnace and annealed under N2 flow at 400°C for 2h.

nodes.characterization_summary: Hierarchical nanoballs assembled from ultrathin nanosheets with diameters 500-800 nm for VSe₂ (maintained after Mo doping), decreased to 500 nm for VSe₂₋ₓ, loosened/collapsed structure for V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂₋ₓ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1b shows a field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) image of the original VSe₂ sample. A hierarchical nanoball configuration was entirely assembled by ultrathin nanosheets with consistent thickness, with sphere diameters ranging from 500 to 800 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Nanosheets possess consistent thickness ≈16.5 nm for V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂₋ₓ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM and AFM results (Figure S1, Supporting Information) indicate that the nanosheets possess consistent thickness (≈16.5 nm).

nodes.characterization_summary: Nanosheets possess consistent thickness ≈16.5 nm for V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂₋ₓ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM and AFM results (Figure S1, Supporting Information) indicate that the nanosheets possess consistent thickness (≈16.5 nm).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows 1T phase VSe₂ (JCPDS no. 89-1641) maintained after Mo doping with decreased intensity and 0.2° shift to lower angle; VSe₂₋ₓ shows peak weakening; V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂₋ₓ shows weaker peaks near 1T to 2H transition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1f shows four XRD patterns of the VSe₂-based samples. For bare VSe₂, five obvious diffraction peaks were indexed to the octahedrally coordinated 1T phase of VSe₂ (JCPDS no. 89-1641).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows A₁g mode at ≈207 cm⁻¹ for pristine VSe₂ 1T phase; after 20% Mo doping additional E₁g (141.7 cm⁻¹) and E₂g¹ (279.2 cm⁻¹) peaks appear; no obvious shifts detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1g illustrates the Raman spectra of the as-prepared various VSe₂-based samples. Pristine VSe₂ exhibited typical A₁g mode peaks of the 1T phase at ≈207 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: 1T phase hexagonal lattice 0.181 nm (110)/(210) planes; uniform bright Mo spots (SA/DA defects) in V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂; single/poly Se vacancies in VSe₂₋ₓ; di-defects (SA Mo surrounded by Se vacancies) in V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂₋ₓ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: From Figure 2a, a well-defined 1T phase hexagonal allocation of V and Se atoms was observed with a 0.181 nm lattice spacing assigned to the (110) and (210) planes of 1T VSe₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Confirms 1T VSe₂ phase for pristine VSe₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This is further supported by the corresponding selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (inset, Figure 2a) and Raman spectra (Figure 1g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform V, Se, Mo elemental distribution across V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂₋ₓ 2D basal plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM (Figure 2i) and the corresponding EDX element mapping images (Figure 2j-l) of the V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂₋ₓ nanoflakes revealed that V, Se, and Mo were uniformly distributed over the 2D basal plane.

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomic ratio V:Mo = 1:0.29 confirmed by ICP-AES for V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂₋ₓ.
nodes.evidence_snippet: conforming the accuracy of the inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectrometry (ICP-AES) results (V:Mo = 1:0.29), as shown in Table S1 (Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: V 2p: 512.7 eV (V³⁺), 513.6 eV (V⁴⁺), 515.8 eV (V⁵⁺) separated by 7.52 eV; Se 3d: 53.4/54.3 eV (Se²⁻); Mo 3d: 228.2/231.3 eV (Mo⁴⁺) positively shifted ~0.8 eV; V:Mo = 1:0.27.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The V 2p₃/₂ peak, three peaks appeared at 512.7, 513.6, and 515.8 eV assigned to the V-Se bonding structures with V³⁺, V⁴⁺, and V⁵⁺, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo K-edge XANES: lower oxidation state and tetrahedral symmetry (pre-edge ~20003 eV) for V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂₋ₓ vs V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂/MoSe₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3e shows that the first derivative of the Mo K pre-edge X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) spectrum of V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂₋ₓ arises from a lower oxidation state than V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂ and MoSe₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo K-edge first-shell Mo-Se distance 2.19 Å (V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂) → 2.22 Å (V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂₋ₓ) due to unsaturated SA Mo coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: When Se vacancy defects formed around the Mo atoms, the first-shell peak from the Mo K-edge of V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂₋ₓ increased to 2.22 Å due to unsaturated coordination of SA Mo.

nodes.characterization_summary: R_ct values: V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂₋ₓ (147.6 Ω acid, 426.6 Ω alkaline, 813.7 Ω neutral) < VSe₂₋ₓ (311.7 Ω) < V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂ (482.5 Ω) < VSe₂ (826.1 Ω).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lowest R_ct was recorded over V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂₋ₓ (147.6 Ω) than those of the VSe₂₋ₓ (311.7 Ω), V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂ (482.5 Ω), and VSe₂ (826.1 Ω).

nodes.characterization_summary: C_dl values from CV: V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂₋ₓ highest at 12.7 mF cm⁻² (acid), 23.9 mF cm⁻² (alkaline), 14.1 mF cm⁻² (neutral) vs VSe₂₋ₓ (8.8), V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂ (6.3), VSe₂ (2.2 mF cm⁻² acid).
nodes.evidence_snippet: V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂₋ₓ yields an extremely high C_dl value up to 12.7 mF cm⁻² in acidic media, considerably larger than those of VSe₂₋ₓ (8.8 mF cm⁻²), V₀.₈Mo₀.₂Se₂ (6.3 mF cm⁻²), and VSe₂ (2.2 mF cm⁻²).
